cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet in Judah, is passing along a message from the LORD, and it is heavy. Judah's sin isn't scribbled in pencil. It's written with an iron stylus and engraved with a diamond point. Friend, that is NOT a sticky note on the fridge.

cards.question: Judah's sin is engraved with a diamond point. Where does the LORD say it's engraved?

answers.text: On their hearts and their altars
On their foreheads and their hands
On their doorposts and their gates

cards.text: And it's not just one generation. Someone else remembers those altars and Asherah poles by the green trees and on the high hills.

cards.question: The LORD says that even Judah's ___ remember their altars and Asherah poles.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out, "O My mountain in the countryside," and He names the problem. It's the sin of their high places, within all their borders.

cards.question: Because of the sin of the high places, what will the LORD do with Judah's wealth and all its treasures?

cards.text: It gets worse. Judah will let go of the inheritance the LORD gave them, and the LORD will enslave them to their enemies.

cards.question: Where will Judah be enslaved to its enemies?

answers.text: In a land they do not know
Back in the land of Egypt

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells Judah that the anger they kindled will burn out soon.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Cursed is the man who trusts in mankind, who makes mere flesh his strength and turns his heart from the LORD." That's like leaning your whole weight on a cookie stamper, and friend, I would FOLD.

cards.question: The LORD says the man who trusts in mankind will be like what?

cards.text: That shrub lives in the parched places of the desert, in a salt land where no one lives. If that place had online reviews, it'd be one star, and the whole review just says "No."

cards.question: True or false: The man who is like a shrub in the desert will not see when prosperity comes.

cards.text: Then the LORD flips it around: "But blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in Him."

cards.question: The man who trusts in the LORD is like a tree planted by the ___.

cards.text: When the heat comes, this tree does not fear, and its leaves are always green. Meanwhile, I sweat through my apron just preheating the OVEN.

cards.question: Why can the tree by the waters stay green when the heat comes?

answers.text: It sends its roots toward the stream
It grows in the shade of the hills
It only grows in the cool season

cards.question: True or false: In a year of drought, the tree by the waters stops producing fruit.

cards.text: Now the LORD says the heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure. Friend, my heart says "just ONE more cookie" every single night, and it has NEVER meant one.

cards.question: The heart is so deceitful that the LORD asks, "Who can understand it?" So who searches the heart?
The LORD examines the ___ to reward a man by what his ___ deserve.

cards.text: Then the LORD paints a strange picture: a partridge hatching eggs it did not lay. Friend, that's the coworker who presents YOUR slides in the meeting.

cards.question: Who does the LORD say is like a partridge hatching eggs it did not lay?

answers.text: A man who makes a fortune unjustly
A man who leaves his father's house
A man who works on the Sabbath

cards.question: True or false: The man who makes a fortune unjustly keeps his riches all his days.

cards.text: Then the words turn into prayer. A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary, and the LORD is the hope of Israel.
All who abandon the LORD will be put to shame, and the ones who turn away get written down. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, so I know EXACTLY what they're written in.

cards.question: All who turn away from the LORD will be written in the ___.
The ones who turn away have abandoned the LORD. In this prayer, what is He called?

cards.text: Now Jeremiah prays for himself: "Heal me, O LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for You are my praise." Then he tells the LORD what people keep saying to him, and spoiler, it is NOT "Great message, Jeremiah!"

cards.question: What do people keep saying to Jeremiah about the word of the LORD?

answers.text: They want it to come now

cards.text: They're tapping their watch at a PROPHET. But Jeremiah says he hasn't run away from being the LORD's shepherd, and the LORD knows his words were spoken in His presence.

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah tells the LORD that he has desired the day of despair.
Jeremiah asks the LORD not to become a terror to him. In the day of disaster, he calls the LORD his ___.
Jeremiah prays about the people persecuting him. What does he ask for when it comes to shame?

answers.text: Shame for them but not for him
Shame for him but not for them
No shame for anyone at all

cards.text: Same goes for fear: let them be terrified, but not him. And he ends with this: "Bring upon them the day of disaster and shatter them with double destruction."

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Jeremiah... it is heavy." / "Judah's sin isn't scribbled in pencil." / "It's written with an iron stylus..." / "Friend, that is NOT a sticky note on the fridge."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says Jeremiah is a prophet in Judah. That fact comes from outside the passage, but the card cites only Jeremiah 17:1 and gives no reference for it, such as Jeremiah 1:1-2.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The setup line "And it's not just one generation" points straight to the next generation. That gives away "children" on card 4 and rules out "enemies" and "prophets."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks why the tree stays green, and its right answer is that the tree sends its roots toward the stream. Jeremiah 17:8 lists these as separate details and never says that one causes the other.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke "I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, so I know EXACTLY what they're written in" relies on the drawer being full of dust. That gives away the answer "dust" on card 9.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
